text: In those days, as the number of disciples kept growing, the Greek-speaking Jews began to complain against the Hebrews that their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.
So the Twelve called the whole company of disciples together and said, "It is not right for us to give up preaching the word of God in order to wait on tables.

versions.text: So the Twelve called the whole company of disciples together and said, "It is not right for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.
versions.explanation: καταλείψαντας means 'to leave behind, abandon, forsake' — stronger than 'neglect'; the sense is abandoning the ministry of the word for table service.

text: Brothers, choose seven men from among you who are well respected and full of the Spirit and of wisdom, and we will put them in charge of this task,
while we devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word."

This proposal pleased the whole gathering, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, along with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch.
They presented these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
And the word of God kept spreading, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.

versions.text: And the word of God kept spreading; the number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly, and a great many of the priests became obedient to the faith.
versions.explanation: For oral reading, the semicolon breaks the flow; the Greek uses coordinated clauses joined by καί, which read more naturally aloud as 'and'.

text: Now Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
But some men from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians and Alexandrians and others from Cilicia and Asia, stood up and began to argue with Stephen.

versions.text: But some members of the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen—Jews from Cyrene and Alexandria, as well as from Cilicia and Asia—stood up and began to argue with Stephen.
versions.explanation: 'Jews from Cyrene and Alexandria' adds the word 'Jews', which is not in the Greek; the text simply lists Cyrenians and Alexandrians. The long dashes also hinder oral reading.

text: But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.

versions.text: They could not stand up against the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
versions.explanation: 'stand up against' repeats the 'stood up' of verse 9 awkwardly; 'withstand' is clearer, and the connective 'but' preserves the contrast implied by the narrative flow.

text: So they secretly instigated men to say, "We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; they came upon him, seized him, and brought him before the council.
They also produced false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us."
Everyone seated in the council fixed their eyes on him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
